issues.legal_issue: A challenge to preliminary tax-recovery notices cannot succeed by prohibition or quashing unless the authority is entirely without jurisdiction, and a challenge is premature while objections remain available.
material_facts: The challenged orders were preliminary notices commencing recovery by attachment, not final orders.
The affected persons could object to the attachment through the recovery process before final orders were made.
Although the notices cited one legal basis, the court considered that recovery power could exist under another legal basis.
issues.conclusion: The notices and proceedings could not be quashed at that stage because the applicants had not demonstrated a total absence of jurisdiction; citing the wrong legal provision would not suffice if authority to proceed existed under another provision.
issues.legal_principle: A writ of prohibition requires a demonstrated total absence of jurisdiction, although an alternative remedy is not generally a bar to that writ. Preliminary proceedings are premature to quash where the affected persons still have an opportunity to object before final orders. A wrong statutory reference does not invalidate action when the power exists under another provision. The court relied on L. Hazari Mal Kuthiala v. Income-tax Officer, Special Circle, Ambala Cantt., Income-tax Officer, Kolar Circle v. Seghu Buchiah Setty, and P. M. Bharucha v. G. S. Venkatesan, Income-tax Officer, Circle 1, Ward A, Bhavnagar.

rule.if: tax_recovery_writ_challenge and preliminary_recovery_notice and objection_process_still_available and authority_available_under_another_law

predicates.tax_recovery_writ_challenge: The affected persons brought a writ challenge to the commencement of tax-recovery proceedings.
predicates.preliminary_recovery_notice: The authority issued a notice beginning recovery proceedings, with final action still to follow.
predicates.objection_process_still_available: The affected persons could raise objections before the recovery authority before final orders were made.
predicates.authority_available_under_another_law: The authority had power to proceed under a legal basis other than the one cited in the notice.

issues.definition: When a writ challenges a preliminary recovery notice, objections remain available, and the authority has power under another legal basis, the preliminary challenge is not quashed.

issues.legal_issue: Mandamus is unavailable unless the applicant establishes non-compliance with a mandatory duty owed by the authority.
material_facts: The applicants sought mandamus against the recovery authority.
They did not establish that the authority had failed to comply with a mandatory provision imposing an obligation toward them.
issues.conclusion: No occasion arose to issue mandamus because the applicants had not shown non-compliance with a mandatory provision or an unperformed obligation owed to them.
issues.legal_principle: Mandamus requires a showing that a mandatory provision has not been complied with and that an obligation toward the applicant has consequently not been carried out.

predicates.mandamus_sought: The applicant asked a court to compel an authority to act.
predicates.mandatory_duty_breach_shown: The applicant established that the authority failed to comply with a mandatory duty owed to the applicant.

issues.definition: When mandamus is sought but no breach of a mandatory duty owed to the applicant is shown, mandamus is not issued.

issues.legal_issue: A recovery officer may exercise recovery functions through the statutory succession of offices, while a factual objection to the officer's authorization that was not raised earlier cannot first be raised on appeal.
material_facts: The Additional Personal Assistant to the Collector was functioning as the tax recovery officer.
The applicants had not earlier objected that this officer lacked the required authorization.
The court held that the relevant statutory provisions could transfer the predecessor recovery officer's functions to a Collector, Additional Collector, or properly authorized officer.
The court left open the applicants' ability to raise before the recovery officer the factual question whether the required notification had been made.
issues.conclusion: The applicants could not raise the authorization objection for the first time on appeal, and the court found no flaw in the High Court's reasoning; the factual question of the required notification remained open for determination by the recovery officer.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied section 8(1) of the General Clauses Act, 1897, section 13(1) of the Finance Act, 1950, and sections 2(44) and 221 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, together with the recovery provision set out in the judgment as section 222(1). These provisions allowed recovery functions to devolve to a Collector, Additional Collector, or an officer authorized by the State Government. A factual objection not raised earlier could not be introduced for the first time on appeal, though the question of notification could be raised before the recovery officer.

predicates.tax_recovery_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning tax-recovery proceedings.
predicates.recovery_officer_claims_authority_throug: The officer performing recovery functions relies on the transfer of those functions from a predecessor office or on authorization to perform them.
predicates.authorization_objection_not_raised_earli: The affected persons did not previously object that the officer lacked the required authorization.

issues.definition: In a tax-recovery appeal, when the recovery officer relies on successor or delegated authority and the affected persons did not raise an authorization objection earlier, the new factual objection is left for initial determination by the recovery authority.

issues.legal_issue: An allegedly invalid part of an attachment does not deprive the recovery officer of jurisdiction to consider objections to the attachment when no sale or other final recovery action has occurred.
material_facts: Some recovery certificates had been held invalid because they were issued after the assessee's death.
The challenged action involved attachment of property, and no property had been sold and no action had been taken against the applicants personally.
The applicants could raise objections to the attachment before the recovery officer.
issues.conclusion: The allegedly invalid certificates and any resulting unjustified attachment did not affect the officer's jurisdiction to consider objections to the attachment.
issues.legal_principle: Where the action is attachment only, an allegedly illegal or unjustified attachment of some property does not oust the recovery officer's jurisdiction to deal with objections under rule 11 of the Second Schedule to the Income-tax Act, 1961.

rule.if: tax_recovery_attachment_proceeding and attachment_only and some_claims_lack_valid_certificates and objection_process_still_available

predicates.tax_recovery_attachment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an authority's attachment of property to recover tax.
predicates.attachment_only: The authority has attached property but has not sold it or taken another final recovery measure.
predicates.some_claims_lack_valid_certificates: Some of the claims supporting the attachment lack valid recovery certificates.
predicates.objection_process_still_available: The affected persons can still challenge the attachment before the recovery authority.

issues.definition: When a tax-recovery proceeding has reached attachment only, some supporting claims lack valid certificates, and objections remain available, the partial defect does not prevent the authority from considering those objections.

issues.legal_issue: When the department accepts use of the predecessor enactment's recovery procedure, the recovery officer must use that procedure so far as it can be applied.
material_facts: The department stated that it did not object to using the procedure under the predecessor enactment to recover dues from the deceased's assets.
The court therefore did not decide whether using the later procedure imposed an additional burden or disadvantage on the applicants.
issues.conclusion: The recovery officer was directed to use the procedure under the predecessor enactment so far as it was possible to apply it.
issues.legal_principle: In light of the department's concession, the court directed use, so far as possible, of the predecessor enactment's recovery procedure and found it unnecessary to decide whether the later procedure imposed an additional burden.

predicates.tax_recovery_from_deceased_estate: The authority is seeking to recover tax dues from assets of a deceased person.
predicates.department_accepts_predecessor_procedure: The department agrees that the recovery procedure under the predecessor enactment may be used.
predicates.predecessor_procedure_can_be_applied: The predecessor enactment's recovery procedure can be applied to the recovery in question.

issues.definition: When recovery is sought from a deceased person's estate, the department accepts the predecessor procedure, and that procedure can be applied, it is used to the extent possible.
